name: Graph reconstruction conjecture
question: Is each finite simple graph on at least three vertices determined by its vertex-deleted deck?
first_attack: Prove reconstruction for a new graph family
method_title: Replay the object, or mine the census
dispatch_next: The certified mine deck_invariants reads degree sequence and triangle count from decks. Together they separate every graph through 5 vertices and leave 20 excess graphs at 6 vertices. A reconstruction lemma needs a deck invariant strictly stronger than those two.
dispatch_why: The deck_invariants mine shows degree sequence plus triangle count still leaves collisions at 6 vertices. A larger census sits inside the published computational range.

campaign.method: Deck-collision search over certified graph censuses
campaign.hypothesis: Every finite simple graph on at least 3 vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its vertex-deleted deck.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Pick a graph family not yet known to be reconstructible and isolate a lemma that reconstructs a new invariant for it.
campaign.next_experiment: The certified mine deck_invariants reads degree sequence and triangle count from decks. Together they separate every graph through 5 vertices and leave 20 excess graphs at 6 vertices. A reconstruction lemma needs a deck invariant strictly stronger than those two.
campaign.falsification: Two non-isomorphic graphs with identical decks, confirmed by independent canonical forms.
campaign.blocker: Computer verification already reaches at least 11 vertices; novelty has to come from a structural lemma, not from range.

probes.name: Graph reconstruction conjecture
probes.title: Vertex-deck reconstruction for every graph up to N vertices
probes.frontier: Known: verified by computer for all graphs on at most 11 vertices (McKay 1997) and beyond; proved for trees, regular and disconnected graphs (Kelly 1957).

smoke.scope: For every n with 3 <= n <= 6, the 6-vertex census is complete (Burnside-certified) and no two non-isomorphic graphs share a vertex-deleted deck.

deep.scope: For every n with 3 <= n <= 7, the 7-vertex census is complete (Burnside-certified) and no two non-isomorphic graphs share a vertex-deleted deck.

milestones.title: Graph reconstruction verified for every graph on 3-6 vertices
milestones.description: Burnside-certified census of 4, 11, 34 and 156 graphs; all decks pairwise distinct under an independent canonical form. Deep run adds all 1,044 graphs on 7 vertices.

milestones.title: Deck-certified degree and triangle separation through 6 vertices
milestones.scope: Census already known to be reconstructible far beyond 6 vertices; this only ranks coarse invariants
milestones.description: Degree sequence separates through 4 vertices. Degree sequence plus triangle count separates through 5 and leaves 20 excess graphs at 6. Both invariants are recomputed from cards.

formal_statement.encodes: Simple graphs on n ≥ 3 vertices with a deck-matching bijection σ (G − v ≅ H − σv) are isomorphic.

discovery_trail.question: How little of each vertex-deleted card suffices to distinguish small graphs, and where does that compression first fail?

nodes.title: Degree sequence plus a global triangle count leaves collisions
nodes.detail: The earlier exact mine found 20 excess isomorphism classes among six-vertex graphs after grouping by degree sequence and global triangle count. The full graph deck holds more information than this unpaired summary.

nodes.title: Keep each deleted card's degree sequence paired with its motif count
nodes.detail: Define S3(G) as the multiset of pairs (degree sequence of G-v, number of triangles in G-v). The pairing preserves which statistics came from the same card.

nodes.title: Independent complete finite census through seven vertices
nodes.detail: The exact signature distinguishes all 156 six-vertex classes and all 1,044 seven-vertex classes. Completeness follows from a verified class census and an independent Burnside count; it is finite mathematics within established graph-reconstruction ranges.

nodes.title: Two explicit triangle-free graphs share S3 at order eight
nodes.detail: The stored eight-vertex edge lists have identical S3 multisets but different four-cycle counts (2 versus 1). Thus they are nonisomorphic; they are not a counterexample to reconstruction from the full deck.

nodes.title: Adding the per-card four-cycle count separates all 12,346 eight-vertex classes
nodes.detail: S4(G) pairs each card's degree sequence, triangle count and four-cycle count. In a complete 133,632-extension cover it takes 12,346 distinct values, matching Burnside's independently computed class count. Mathematical novelty remains unconfirmed.

nodes.title: Find a nine-vertex collision or certify the next finite class
nodes.detail: Obtain a complete nine-vertex generator or an explicit pair that defeats S4. Before any novelty claim, seek independent mathematical and prior-art review.
